en.template: Compare selling channels for my {location} handmade jewellery business using {price}, {orders}, {costs}, {mix}, {weights} and {quotes}. Show profit after paying my time, upfront cash, customer-acquisition costs and unresolved VAT, returns and product-safety requirements. Keep NOTHS quote-only until I supply its terms and resolve Amazon's published-rate conflict. Plan only; do not create accounts, apply, contact anyone or pay.

phases.title: Read official platform, postage and compliance pages, dated 6 November 2026
phases.note: Etsy, Shopify, Folksy, Not On The High Street and Amazon Handmade fees; Royal Mail UK and EU prices; hallmarking costs
phases.judgment: It caught a postage trap: Royal Mail’s Tracked services advertise compensation, but their terms exclude jewellery. The plan therefore prices Special Delivery by 1pm (£10.85 for up to 500 g, the plan’s default; £9.85 up to 100 g; up to £750 cover) instead of the cheaper service that would not pay out.

phases.title: Build the editable profit workbook and the one-page guide
Recalculate the workbook and check the delivered files
phases.judgment: A separate reviewer read the workbook’s formulas and found two real flaws: setting any platform to zero orders would break its profit, and editing one order cell could silently mislabel the comparison. Both were fixed before the final recalculation, which showed all 505 formulas working with zero errors. Not On The High Street stays marked “Quote needed” rather than being given an invented profit.
